priorities.finding: Request context is the sole train-only feature group with positive aggregate lift (+0.00221), complete coverage, and positive lift on all four temporal holdout days. The already-tested train-fitted user-by-tab cross produced only a small official-validation gain over experiment 1 (+0.000439 primary), so its incremental benefit is directionally positive but below the prior predicted gain and not sufficient to fund broader context interaction expansion. Post-score diagnostics show substantial top-five weakness in high-volume tab 0 (nDCG@5 0.0625; 13,726 rows), tab 6 (nDCG@5 0.1056; 5,170 rows), and hour 16 (nDCG@5 0.3569 despite GAUC 0.6343).
priorities.recommended_action: Retain the existing availability-safe request-context treatment, including the train-fitted user-by-tab cross, but stop feature expansion under the strict early-stopping rule. If one low-cost follow-up is permitted, perform a time-split robustness check focused on tab 0, tab 6, and hour 16 top-five ranking; require a material, repeatable nDCG@5 improvement rather than GAUC alone before continuing.

avoid: Reject user_profile, historical_user_author_affinity, upload_recency, content_duration, item_metadata, historical_author_response, and historical_item_response: each has non-positive training-only primary lift, with especially large stable losses for historical author/item response features. metric_diagnosis: Experiment 3 has credible global within-user ranking discrimination (GAUC 0.6699) and moderate top-five quality (nDCG@5 0.5368), but the aggregate masks concentrated top-five failures. The most consequential weakness is not merely low GAUC: tab 0 combines a sizable sample with extremely poor nDCG@5 (0.0625), while tab 6 also has weak nDCG@5 (0.1056). Rare items are additionally weak in both GAUC (0.4000) and nDCG@5 (0.1700), but have limited support (249 rows). Conversely, some hour slices show acceptable GAUC while weak top-five placement, such as hour 16, confirming that GAUC alone should not drive further investment. The observed gain of experiment 3 over experiment 1 is only +0.000439 primary, following a failed experiment 2 branch, which supports early stopping rather than speculative feature additions.
